title: Nem működik vagy Elromlott? Reporting a Problem

sections.title: A state vs. an event
sections.content: You already know nem működik ("doesn't work") from Unit 16, for a machine that simply isn't doing its job right now: A klíma nem működik. elromlik ("to break down") you already know too, from Unit 15's travel problems. Its past tense, elromlott ("it broke"), reports the actual moment something stopped working — the event, not just the ongoing state. Often both are true at once: Elromlott a zár, ezért nem működik. ("The lock broke, so it doesn't work.")

items.spanish: A szobában nem működik a wifi.
items.english: The wifi doesn't work in the room.
The heating broke in the apartment.

sections.content: Use elromlott to point to the moment something broke (it's a past-tense event), and nem működik to describe how things stand right now (an ongoing state) — you can lead with either one, and often you'll want both.
